text:
anya: heads-up — nightly perf run showing a spike in OOMs for medium/long seq workloads. suspect workspace selection hitting a bigger Triton/cuBLASLt path when FlashAttention opts out.

anya: quick excerpt from the profiler: 
```
model=redwood-medium
batch=8
seqs=256/512/1024 (mixed)
flashattn_workspace_peak=1.1GB (when used)
triton_fallback_workspace_peak=2.3GB
kv_cache_reserve=600MB
slab_alloc_failures=3 -> OOM
```

mike: yikes. was this on the new kernel-chooser thresholds we rolled last week?

anya: yes — the chooser now prefers FlashAttention when pad_ratio < 0.3, but if mixed batch pads push avg pad_ratio above 0.32 we trigger a fallback which increases workspace. essentially oscillation across batches.

mike: do we have the batching histogram for the job? curious how often we cross that threshold.

anya: attaching a short summary inline: avg_pad_pct over last hour: [0.12,0.18,0.34,0.29,0.31,0.33] -> frequent crossings.

mike: ok that explains instability. Two quick mitigations: 1) add hysteresis to kernel chooser (only switch after N consecutive batches). 2) cap workspace growth by slab-aware upper bound so fallback cannot steal KV reserve.

dina: +1 on hysteresis. also we should compute per-batch estimated workspace before choosing kernel. simple estimator: est_ws = base + batch_size * seq_len * hidden_state * coeff. keep coeff conservative for Triton.

elaine: can we show the estimator? I want to ensure it accounts for kv_cache per-request.

dina: example pseudocode:
```
# naive estimator
est_flash = base_flash + B * avg_L * H * k_flash
est_triton = base_triton + B * avg_L * H * k_triton
if est_flash < slab_free * safety_frac: pick flash
elif est_triton < slab_free * safety_frac: pick triton
else: pick smallest and mark for eviction
```

ricardo: two notes: 1) slab_free must exclude KV cache reserved region. 2) safety_frac should be dynamic: higher when eviction pressure observed.

mike: on the allocator side, we can expose a "proactive_reserve" call that marks X bytes untouchable for KV use during selection window. then either commit or release. reduces races.

anya: logged a small repro in CI: model=redwood-medium, batch pattern [8,4,16] with mixed seqs. I can attach flamegraphs.

ops-bot: deploy-notice: rolled kernel-chooser v2.3 to canary at 1876503000 by @mike :rocket:

mike: for immediate triage I reverted the hysteresis change in canary and added a guarding cap: kernel-chooser will not select fallback if est_workspace - current_allocation > 0.7 * slab_free. should reduce sudden jumps.

elaine: can we also instrument kv-cache eviction counts in the trace? want to correlate OOMs with eviction-induced misses.

anya: added a lightweight metric: kv_evictions_per_min. on the failing runs it spikes to ~120/min before crash.

dina: long-term: propose a small stateful predictor that keeps sequence-length percentiles per route (p50/p90/p99) and uses them to pick batch heuristics + kernel. That avoids reacting to short bursts.

ricardo: agree. also consider a tiny per-slab soft cap for workspace allocations: if slab_frag > X% then prefer kernels with smaller contiguous workspace even if slightly slower.

mike: next steps (action items):
- anya: attach flamegraphs + CI repro and mark failing CI job (done)
- dinA: implement estimator and hysteresis toggle behind feature flag (in progress)
- ricardo: add slab_proactive_reserve API + metric for eviction pressure (queued)
- elaine: add kv_evictions_per_min to dashboards and create alert when >50/min (todo)

anya: also: watch out for cuBLASLt behavior — its workspace query sometimes returns transiently large requirements on certain hardware; treat one-off spikes as noisy unless they persist for >3 batches.

mike: good point. add persistence window for workspace queries. and add a fast-path fallback: if cuBLASLt query suddenly > 1.5x historical p95, ignore it once.

elaine: can we simulate mixed padding in the memsim harness? would be useful to validate heuristics without touching prod.

anya: yes. I'll add a memsim scenario that randomizes seq lengths with configurable burstiness and KV occupancy.

ops-bot: canary-deploy status: kernel-chooser v2.3 at canary healthy at 1876504500 (0 failures in last 10m).

mike: thanks everyone. plan is: merge estimator behind flag, run memsim stress, flip on hysteresis if stable, then roll to small percentage. keep the proactive_reserve opt-in for enterprise customers for now.

ricardo: FYI I'll also add a small debug trace when slab_alloc fails that dumps the per-slab LRU sizes and pending workspace reservations — should make root-cause postmortems faster.

anya: great. I'll post the CI artifacts in the thread when ready. :eyeglasses:
